topic.title: Generative Priors for Imaging Inverse Problems
topic.overview: Inverse imaging reconstructs an unknown image from incomplete or degraded measurements, such as blur or missing pixels. This topic uses learned generative priors to constrain the many images that could explain those measurements. It studies posterior sampling, regularization, measurement consistency, and ways to control bias introduced by approximate likelihoods or implicit models.
topic.whyItMatters: A visually plausible reconstruction can contain unsupported detail, so image quality must be evaluated together with agreement with observations and uncertainty. Prior strength, measurement assumptions, and sampling schedules all influence whether a reconstruction reflects the evidence or the model’s expectations.
topic.evolution: A 2004 representative formally connects learning with regularization for ill-posed inverse problems. Recent work brings diffusion priors and latent posterior sampling into image restoration. A 2026 energy-based approach learns normalized posterior densities across linear measurement conditions, enabling adaptive sampling, correction steps, and estimation of degradation operators within its framework.
openQuestions: How can uncertainty reveal details supplied mainly by the prior rather than measurements?
When do weaker generative priors offer better reconstruction reliability or efficiency?
